title: Mijn familie, mijn buurt
summary: Capstone: family and neighborhood portrait, plus mijn verhaal layer 3

blocks.title: Week 3, alles bij elkaar
blocks.body: This week: family plus the warm *-je*, the **-e rule** for adjectives, possessives (*mijn, jouw, zijn, haar, ons/onze, hun*), and your own *buurt*. Time to use it all — and grow your story further.

blocks.prompt: Which is correct — 'the nice city' (stad is de)?
blocks.explain: De-words always take -e: de leuke stad.

pairs.left: een leuk huis — a nice house (indefinite)
pairs.right: mijn leuke huis — my nice house (possessive)
pairs.note: Possessives (mijn, jouw, zijn, haar, ons, onze, hun) act like definite articles for adjectives — always add -e, even with a het-word.

blocks.prompt: Combine a possessive, an adjective, and a family member or place.

blocks.scene: You tell Daan about your family and your neighborhood.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Dit is mijn zusje — heel grappig, en heel aardig.
lines.en: This is my little sister — really funny, and really kind.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.en: Nice! And where does she live?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: In onze oude buurt, vlakbij een gezellig plein.
lines.en: In our old neighborhood, close to a cozy square.
lines.spotlight: onze oude buurt — buurt is de, always -e.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: En jouw huis — is dat ook gezellig?
lines.en: And your house — is that cozy too?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Heel gezellig, ja. Ons kleine huis, maar wel heel warm.
lines.en: Very cozy, yes. Our small house, but very warm.
lines.spotlight: ons kleine huis — ons + adjective always takes -e, even for a het-word.

questions.q: Why is it 'ons kleine huis' and not 'ons klein huis'?
options: Possessives always trigger -e, like definite articles
There's no rule, both are fine

blocks.title: Mijn verhaal — hoofdstuk 3
blocks.prompt: Add your family and your buurt to your growing self-intro. Keep last week's layers (name, where you're from, that you're learning Dutch, your daily routine) and add your family and neighborhood, using possessives (mijn/onze/haar) and -e adjectives.
Three weeks in — knap gedaan! Family, buurt, adjectives, possessives — all in the bag. Write one sentence celebrating what you learned this week, in Dutch if you can.
